texto: In the kitchen in front of two other servants, Valeria throws the white apron in Lupe's face; Lupe slowly takes it off her face, folds it calmly and puts it on the table, looking Valeria in the eye; the servants gasp.
Later, alone by the wood-fired stove, old Doña Chela grabs Lupe's arm, looks toward the door to make sure nobody is listening and whispers to her; Lupe's face changes.
In the dark stables, Doña Leonor hands the thick envelope of money to Chuy; he weighs it in his hand and smiles under his mustache, touching the brim of his hat.
From the dark balcony, Valeria lowers her phone and looks down toward the stables, frowning, troubled, slowly realizing what her mother is doing.
Emiliano breaks the rusty padlock with a hammer, the chain falls to the floor; Lupe, holding her breath, pushes the old wooden door open with a long creak.

In the dusty room, Lupe kneels and pulls the old dusty suitcase from under the bed; she opens it: it is full of a woman's folded clothes; she touches them with trembling hands; Emiliano watches from the door.

Flashback with warm soft faded tones, at night: Carmen, alone and frightened, writes the letter by candle light, hides it in a small wooden box, then freezes, hearing heavy footsteps outside the door.

Night, in Lupe's room the lamp suddenly goes out; the dark silhouette of a man in a cowboy hat appears behind the small window and knocks on the glass three times; Lupe pulls the blanket to her chest, terrified.
Lupe runs barefoot out into the dark corridor and crashes into Rodrigo, who is leaning against the wall with a glass of whisky; he smiles with contempt and blocks her way.
Next morning in the study, the notary takes the big old iron key out of his leather folder and places it in Lupe's open hand; she closes her fingers around it.

At night, Lupe opens the chapel door with the old iron key; she and Emiliano walk in with the lantern and stop in front of the plain stone tomb with no name; Emiliano crouches and wipes the dust off the stone.
Behind them, at the chapel door, Doña Leonor appears holding her own lantern, her face half lit, perfectly calm and cold, her red nails on the door frame.
Lupe turns and faces Doña Leonor, tears in her eyes but standing firm; Leonor walks closer and leans to her ear; slow push-in on Lupe's face as she freezes in shock.
